land.text: Italian Somaliland, independent on 1 July 1960 ('Italian Somaliland followed on 1 July')

predecessors.note: The italian-africa dossier is another af-08 part.

land.text: British Somaliland, independent on 26 June 1960 ('British Somaliland obtained independence on 26 June 1960')

predecessors.note: British Somaliland was independent for five days (26 June - 1 July 1960) before the union; it has no Cliopatria row of its own and no dossier.

capitals.name: Mogadishu
capitals.note: 'the capital and largest city, Mogadishu'. The page records no change of capital.

keyframe_review.note: 646,088 km2 for 1960-2023 against the infobox land area 637,657 km2 (no year; ratio 1.01). The union of Italian Somaliland and British Somaliland (the present Somaliland) in 1960. The shape is the de jure country for all 64 years: Somaliland's 1991 secession is carried by the ledger's loss event (rule 5/7 style), and Puntland (1998) and Jubaland are federal member states inside Somalia, not separate polities.
646,088 km2, identical to 1960-2023: the Federal Republic as 'reformed' in August 2012; Somaliland remains outside its control (ledger 1991 loss).

region.text: Italian Somaliland, which 'followed on 1 July' British Somaliland into independence

ledger.note: 1960: Italian Somaliland becomes independent and unites with British Somaliland as the Somali Republic. 'British Somaliland obtained independence on 26 June 1960, and Italian Somaliland followed on 1 July, with the two uniting to form the Somali Republic.'
1960: British Somaliland joins the union on 1 July. The same sentence of the Somalia page as the founding; the land is the former British protectorate, the present Somaliland.

1969: Siad Barre's Supreme Revolutionary Council takes power and renames the country the Somali Democratic Republic. 'Six days later, on 21 October, General Siad Barre led a military coup'; 'The SRC subsequently renamed the country to the Somali Democratic Republic.' The page does not date the renaming; the year is the coup's (the intro says 'seized power in 1969'); the intro dates it: Siad Barre 'seized power in 1969 and established the Somali Democratic Republic' (confidence raised to 2 by reviewer af-08-f, 2026-10-19; no month on the page).

region.text: the Ogaden, the Somali-inhabited region of Ethiopia

ledger.note: 1977: Somalia and the Western Somali Liberation Front invade the Ogaden. The page dates the invasion to 12, 13 or 23 July 1977; 'Within less than a month of the invasion, 70% of the Ogaden had been taken by the SNA-WSLF force' and 'Gode was captured by the Somalis on July 25'; Jijiga fell on 12 September 1977 and Ethiopia held 'only about 10% of the Ogaden'.

region.text: the Ogaden, retaken by Ethiopia with Soviet and Cuban help

ledger.note: 1978: Ethiopia retakes the Ogaden. Jijiga was retaken on 5 March, Siad Barre 'ordered the SNA to retreat into Somalia on 9 March 1978' and 'On 23 March 1978, the Ethiopian government declared that the last border post had been regained, thus ending the war.' No border change followed.

region.text: 'the northern former British portion of the country declared its independence as the Republic of Somaliland in May 1991'

ledger.note: 1991: the north breaks away after Siad Barre falls. 'In 1991, the Barre administration was ousted by a coalition of clan-based opposition groups'; Somaliland declared independence in May 1991 (the page gives the month, not the day). Unrecognised but de facto independent to 2024; the page gives no boundary, so the former British protectorate (the Natural Earth Somaliland polygon) is the researcher's reading.

2012: the Transitional Federal Government gives way to the Federal Republic. The TFG 'was the internationally recognised government of Somalia until 20 August 2012'; 'A new provisional constitution was passed in August 2012, reforming Somalia as a federation.' Puntland (1998) and the other member states are inside the federation.

wars.name: Ogaden War
wars.outcome: Infobox 'Ethiopian victory': Somali forces took 70 percent of the Ogaden within a month of the invasion and Jijiga on 12 September 1977, then were pushed out by the Ethiopian-Cuban counterattack of 1 February 1978 (Jijiga 5 March, Degehabur 8 March); the border did not change.
wars.note: The Soviet Union 'withdrew its support for Somalia and backed Ethiopia instead'; Somalia expelled Soviet advisers on 13 November 1977.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a surveyed or treaty frontier: the Ethiopian frontier (Ogaden, Haud returned to Ethiopia 'in 1948') and the Kenyan frontier (the Northern Frontier District, granted to Kenya) are colonial-era administrative lines that Somalia contested, and since 1991 the land boundary with Somaliland and between the member states is de facto only.

sources.title: Somalia

sources.title: Ogaden War

notes: Cliopatria: two shapes (1960-2023, 2024) of 646,088 km2, identical; modern countries Somalia, Somaliland, Kenya (the south reaches 1.64 S, which clips Kenya's boundary at the grid). The shape is the union of Italian and British Somaliland and so contains Somaliland through 2024; the ledger loss of 1991 is the correction, and the rendering agent should draw Somaliland as its own state from then (the scope names it; a 'somaliland' dossier is needed, as is one for British Somaliland's five days of independence). Not on the two pages (budget 1-2): Ethiopia's 2006 invasion has no end date or extent ('At the end of 2006, a US-backed Ethiopian invasion overthrew the Islamic Courts Union'); the Northern Frontier District and Haud transfers are pre-1960; Jubaland, South West State and Hirshabelle are federal member states (2014-2015 on the page), Puntland was 'established' in 1998 under Abdullahi Yusuf - treated as autonomous parts, not secessions; the Somali Civil War has no page in this run. Rulers: the page names Aden Abdullah Osman Daar, Shermarke (president 1967-1969), Siad Barre (1969-1991), Abdullahi Yusuf (from 2004), Sharif Sheikh Ahmed (2009-2012), Hassan Sheikh Mohamud (2012-2017, 2022-), Farmajo (2017-2022) without a complete list, so no ruler strip. Slug note: counterpart 'italian-africa' is the af-08 dossier for Italian Somaliland; 'british-africa' is the af-08 dossier that carries British Somaliland until 1960 (the Cliopatria British Africa row neighbours Somalia in 1960). Native name: not on the page.
